value.body: Telecom engineers plan, install and maintain mobile, fibre and other communication networks. They work for telecom operators, equipment vendors, tower and fibre companies and network-services firms, and the day can involve field installation, network monitoring, testing and troubleshooting.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / B.E. in ECE or a related branch

items.label: Common work areas
items.value: RF planning, network operations (NOC), fibre / transmission, installation and testing

items.label: GATE EC paper (2024)
items.source: GATE 2024 Statistical and Performance Report (IISc Bengaluru)

items.label: Students in Electronics & Communication Engineering
items.note: All levels; AISHE lists ~5.7 lakh more under 'Electronics Engineering' separately. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often join as graduate engineer trainees at network-services firms and equipment vendors, or as field and NOC engineers. Telecom PSUs recruit through their own exams or GATE in some years.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Basics of RF, transmission and networking

value.title: At a glance
items: Field roles involve travel and on-call work.
Common next steps: RF or network optimisation specialist, network planning, or project lead.
5G and fibre rollouts drive much of the current work.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
